maria (runtime): FYI: noticed a regression on TP+PP workloads after yesterday's kernelselect tweak. All-reduce tail latency up ~18% on NVLink machines.

maria (runtime): baseline (before tweak) vs after: similar perf on PCIe boxes, NVLink nodes show higher variance and intermittent spikes. suspect decision heuristic is choosing a 'cross-node-friendly' kernel that actually serializes some NVLink paths.

devin (infra): any quick numbers or traces? can you paste the perf counters or flame?

maria (runtime): pasted perf sample from run on 8xA100 NVLink (DGX-like):
```
wall: 1200s total tokens=1.2M
avg token latency: 45ms -> 53ms (post-change)
allreduce avg: 6.2ms -> 9.1ms
max allreduce tail: 32ms -> 120ms spikes
comm/compute overlap dropped from ~68% -> ~44%
KV cache eviction rate: +12% (more cross-shard syncs)
```

jiayi (ml-runtime): interesting that PCIe unaffected. sounds like the kernel selector is preferring a fused kernel that assumes local NVLink bandwidth will hide a serial path, but in our topology code the ribbon binding can route across PCIe for certain ringlets. do we have route maps for those repro runs?

maria (runtime): attach topology dump (short): ring0: nvlink local, ring1: nvlink local, ring2: cross-socket via pcie, ring3: efa (intra-rack). The scheduler picked the kernel that expects full nvlink for ring2.

perf-bot: perf dashboard: https://perf.redwood.example/runs/235678-pp-tp-regress (attached heatmap). showing correlation between kernel version 3.12-selector and spikes.

devin (infra): can we repro with `KERSEL_FORCE=legacy` or `--kernelselect=prior`? if that fixes it we can hotfix selector heuristics.

maria (runtime): quick test with `--kernelselect=legacy` reverted allreduce back to ~6.5ms and tail spikes gone. KV eviction also normalized. so kernel selection is a strong suspect.

jiayi (ml-runtime): notes: legacy kernel avoids a shared buffer that on NVLink nodes causes a lock under certain allreduce fragment sizes. new selector picks fused path for >16k sequence length; our batch probing changed threshold to 12k accidentally.

anthony (sre): rollout plan? is this in prod-hosted API? we saw a small bump in error budget for a few customers.

maria (runtime): it's in staged dedicated capacity pool and one prod region (canary). impact limited but visible for TP+PP heavy customers. recommend reverting selector change and backporting fix to kernel for next patch.

devin (infra): I'll open a canary rollback PR for selector config (exp flag) and push to the affected pool. can we add a runtime guard that forces `kernelselect=legacy` when topology contains mixed NVLink/PCIe rings?

jiayi (ml-runtime): yes we should do topology-aware override. quick heuristic: if any ring uses cross-socket PCIe for ring id < N then prefer legacy. need unit tests.

maria (runtime): also saw KV cache thrash pattern: smaller batches after selector change caused more frequent prefix misses leading to extra KV sync across PP shards. batching heuristics bump is a co-contributor.

perf-bot: small note: KV cache eviction traces: https://perf.redwood.example/traces/kv-evict/235678 (shows eviction timestamps aligned with allreduce spikes).

anthony (sre): can we mitigate quickly via config? e.g., increase batching tolerance to keep batch sizes stable until kernel patch lands.

devin (infra): yes, will stage config: `batching.window_ms += 5` and `min_batch_tokens += 64` for canary pools. will push in 10m.

maria (runtime): thanks. I'll prepare a bug for kernelselect: revert threshold change and add topology-aware check + unit to detect nvlink/pcie mixed rings.

jiayi (ml-runtime): I'll prototype kernel fix to avoid the problematic shared buffer when comm path uses PCIe; fallback path preserves fused math but decouples buffer lock. rough ETA 48h.

deploy-bot: deploy started: canary config bump to pool 'dedicated-eu-02' at 2026-03-18T15:34:00Z :rocket:

anthony (sre): I'll monitor the canary metrics and set alert for allreduce tail > 80ms. ping me if we see regression post-deploy.

maria (runtime): one extra note: add a perf regression test in our nightly: run synthetic TP+PP model with mixed topologies (nvlink/pcie/efa) and assert allreduce p99 < 40ms.

devin (infra): agreed. will add to the infra matrix.

maria (runtime): thanks all. I'll file the kernelselect rollback PR and link the regression ticket.

jiayi (ml-runtime): thx. rough todo: (1) rollback selector threshold, (2) topology guard, (3) kernel buffer fix, (4) batching tweaks in canary.

anthony (sre): good plan. :thumbsup:

maria (runtime): closing loop here once PRs are merged. will post follow-up with perf numbers.
